key_insight: Multimodal EHR foundation models can benefit from careful latent compression and gated cross-attention, but simply adding extra clinical modalities does not automatically improve prediction.
clinical_relevance: For AI systems used in hospitals, the way ECGs, X-rays, and notes are fused with EHR data may matter as much as the modalities themselves for reliable ICU risk prediction.
method: Conditioned an autoregressive EHR foundation model on auxiliary modalities using modality-specific latent compression.
Used gated cross-attention with temporal alignment to integrate ECG waveforms, chest X-rays, and clinical notes.
Compared compression strategies and pretrained encoder choices through controlled ablations.
evidence_signal: On MIMIC-IV, the authors report that the best latent-compression setup outperformed both uncompressed cross-attention and mean pooling, with stronger pretrained encoders giving better results within each modality.
watch_item: Adding multimodal inputs alone may fail to beat an EHR-only baseline, so fusion design and clinical evaluation must be handled carefully.
paper_title: Autoregressive EHR Foundation Models with Multimodal Inputs
